verses.text: These are the words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. In the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year, I was in the royal city of Susa.
Hanani, one of my brothers, came from Judah with some other men. I asked them about the Jews who had survived and were left from those taken prisoner, and about Jerusalem.
They told me, "The people who survived and are left in the province are in great trouble and shame. The wall of Jerusalem is broken down, and its gates have been burned."
When I heard this, I sat down and cried. For several days I mourned, went without food, and prayed to the God of heaven.
I said, "LORD, God of heaven, please hear me. You are the great and amazing God. You keep your covenant of faithful love with those who love you and obey your commands.

Please listen and open your eyes to hear the prayer I, your servant, am praying to you day and night for the people of Israel, your servants. I confess the sins we Israelites have done against you. Yes, I and my father's family have sinned.
We have done very wrong against you. We have not obeyed the commands, rules, and laws you gave your servant Moses.
Please remember what you told your servant Moses: 'If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the nations.

But if you come back to me and obey my commands, then even if your people have been scattered to the farthest edge of the sky, I will gather them from there. I will bring them to the place I have chosen as a home for my name.'
They are your servants and your people. You rescued them with your great power and your strong hand.

Lord, please listen to the prayer of your servant, and to the prayers of your servants who love to honor your name. Please let me succeed today, and make the king kind to me." At that time I served wine to the king.
